review_candidates.description: Job Title:  Executive Director, Lidè Haiti Location: Hybrid: the position requires in-person presence with the LIDE team and communities in both the North (Gonaïves) and South (Les Coteaux) of Haiti to ensure the success of programs; in Port-au-Prince for representing the organization to the government and other collaborators as well as overseeing the administrative team based there; and events with board members, donors, diaspora stakeholders, and others in the US, Canada, Europe and potentially beyond to spread the good word and ensure the organization's financial success. Type:  Full-time, Exempt Reports to:  Board of Directors Closing Date:  Sept. 30 th , 2026 Salary:  $85,000–$105,000 USD, commensurate with experience    Overview: Founded in 2014, Lidè Haiti has spent over a decade accompanying adolescent girls ages 9–19 in remote, underserved communities across Gonaïves (Artibonite) and Les Coteaux (South), currently serving 590 girls year-round across 8 sites (up to 700, security permitting), plus 40 alumnae scholars ages 20–24. Our model integrates three pillars:  Arts-Based Education and Creative Play (building literacy, voice, and confidence); Wellbeing Support Services, and Family and Community Engagement, using art activities to spark inner strength and joy. We are driven by our vision for a Haiti where every girl can play, create, learn, and lead.   We aim to grow community connections with families, local civil society, and philanthropic partners.   Our Mission To accompany Haitian girls in underserved communities as they improve their learning, health, and well-being through art-centered educational programs in safe and nurturing environments.   Our Values Mutual Aid, Integrity, Inclusive Creativity, Respect, Accountability, Community Collaboration, Lifelong Learning and Empathy   Primary Responsibilities:   Leadership and Management: • Oversees and works first and foremost with the In-Country Director and closely with each department head, including—arts, development, programs, communications, accounting, and operations. • Champions Lidè Haiti’s three-pillar model—Arts-Based Education and Creative Play, Wellbeing Support Services, and Family and Community Engagement—ensuring alignment across all program areas. • Embraces the role of mentor and guide to foster collaboration, setting the stage for   success. •  Stewards the annual operating budget of $1.2M USD, with plans to scale as the organization grows. • Provides strategic guidance to department heads, setting annual goals, along with the   finance committee of the Board of Directors, and establishing effective community service   standards for program staff. • Ensures ongoing alignment with the mission, vision, and core values; strategic evolution of   programming informed by rigorous evaluation; and efficient systems development for   streamlining finance, administration, fundraising, and communications. • Leads, coaches, nurtures skills, promotes self-sufficiency, and preserves the   organization's foundation and strengths developed in our first decade, while building   infrastructure for lasting organizational capacity. Fundraising and Financial Management: •  Builds on and cultivates ever greater conditions for fundraising success, including   soliciting major gifts and invitations for proposals. • Ensures prudent, respectful use and efficient engagement of all organizational assets   Including facilities, people, networks, reputation, and good will. • Identifies, establishes, and nurtures meaningful relationships with donors who share our   vision. • Expands and diversifies our donor base, securing funding to sustain, strengthen, and grow   programs so that together we can support every girl on her path to thrive.   Public Relations: •  Along with the Board of Directors, shares the role of being the public face of the   organization, attending and hosting fundraising and public events to share our story, rallies   support for the cause and demonstrates genuine support for the community at large. • Actively engages and energizes the Board Directors, committees, emeritus Board    members, partnering organizations, and funders. • Maintains a working knowledge of significant developments and trends in Haiti, the non-   profit sector, and relevant programmatic advances especially with respect to informal   educational curriculum.   Compliance and Best Practices: ·       Complies with all laws and regulations and creates systems to ensure the organization is meeting high standards for the industry and region. Develops robust systems and processes to uphold industry best practices, setting the bar for excellence in everything we do.   Board Development: Attends all Board meetings and relevant committee meetings, preparing materials and updates in advance to support informed decision-making. Develops, maintains, and supports a strong Board of Directors; serves as ex-officio on relevant committees; seeks and builds board involvement with strategic direction for ongoing local operations. Works closely with the Board Chair to support the individual in this role. Fosters a culture of engagement and accountability, empowering the Board to make a meaningful difference in the lives of the girls we serve. Provides the Board of Directors with regular reports on programmatic, financial, and operational performance to support informed governance and decision-making.   Strategic Planning: Leads the implementation of our strategic plan, driving innovation and growth to achieve our long-term goals. Continually drives strategic planning, fundraising, and stakeholder relationships to achieve the organization’s mission, goals and outcomes. Qualifications: Education: Bachelor's degree required; Master's or non-profit management training preferred.   Experience: •   Direct experience working in Haiti is critical for success. • 3-5 years-experience in non-profit management, including a proven track record in    successful fundraising. Candidates with less experience will be considered if they can    demonstrate relevant success. • Experience coordinating teams in multiple settings (i.e. hybrid and virtual) preferred. • Proficiency in French, Haitian Kreyol, and English. • Experience with Financial Management and Customer Relationship Management (CRM)    platforms/software. • Experience with financial oversight and regulatory compliance across U.S. and Haiti operations, including U.S. nonprofit reporting requirements (Form 990) and in-country banking and financial systems. • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to lead diverse, cross-cultural teams and adapt quickly in a dynamic operating environment. • Experience building relationships with team members and partners over virtual platforms    and in-person engagement. • Willingness to travel quarterly to program sites (conditions permitting).  • Valid U.S. visa We are an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion.   We thank all applicants for your interest.    Those selected for an interview will be contacted.
